en.title: Trust and Obey
en.author: John H. Sammis
stanzas:
When we [E]walk with the Lord in the [B7]light of His [E]Word,
What a [E]glory He [A]sheds on our [B7]way!
While we [E]do His good will, He a[B7]bides with us [E]still,
And with [A]all who will [B7]trust and o[E]bey.

Not a shadow can rise, not a cloud in the skies,
But His smile quickly drives it away;
Not a doubt or a fear, not a sigh or a tear,
Can abide while we trust and obey.

Not a burden we bear, not a sorrow we share,
But our toil He doth richly repay;
Not a grief or a loss, not a frown or a cross,
But is blessed if we trust and obey.

But we never can prove the delights of His love
Until all on the altar we lay;
For the favor He shows, for the joy He bestows,
Are for them who will trust and obey.
en.chorus:
[E]Trust and o[A]bey, for there's [E]no other [B7]way
To be [E]happy in [A]Jesus, but to [B7]trust and o[E]bey.

notes: Text follows Timeless Truths (5 stanzas + refrain), which prints the full Sammis text with the traditional capitalised divine pronouns. Hymnary's representative text (United Methodist Hymnal 1989) omits stanza 2 ("Not a shadow can rise") and lowercases the pronouns; it is otherwise word-for-word the same. Line division is the source's four long lines, so the printed lines pair up against the 6.6.9 D meter hymnary lists (each of lines 1 and 3 is two 6-syllable phrases). Curly apostrophes in the source were rendered as ASCII ' for consistency across the hymnal. Key: hymnary's tune page gives TRUST AND OBEY as F major and Timeless Truths prints it in F; E is the nearest of the guitar keys (1 semitone down) — G (2 up) is the obvious alternative if the maintainer would rather have open-position vi/ii chords than C#m/F#m. Independently cross-checked 2026-08-01 against AmblesideOnline, which prints the same five stanzas in the same order with the same capitalised pronouns, word-for-word; it ends stanza 5's first two lines with full stops where this source has a semicolon and a comma. hymnal.net independently confirms Towner, F major, 3/4 and 6.6.9.6.6.9 with chorus (the same meter as the "6.6.9 D with refrain" recorded here).
